items.title: A record-breaking X-ray flash may reveal the birth of a magnetar
items.summary: Astronomers have found strong evidence that some mysterious, minutes-long X-ray flashes are produced when two neutron stars collide and create a magnetar. One record-setting event glowed in X-rays for nearly 10 minutes, potentially opening a new way to find these extreme cosmic mergers.

items.summary: Co-design projects give stakeholders a seat at the table, including them as members of the design team, but few studies have evaluated whether they feel heard. items.title: Ocean heatwaves are hiding months of extra warming
items.summary: Marine heatwaves may be only the most intense part of much longer warming events, with elevated temperatures sometimes lingering for months. items.title: E. coli survives longer in poultry-amended Georgia onion soils, two-year study finds
items.summary: New research suggests that poultry litter-based soil amendments and weather conditions, particularly extreme weather events, may influence how long bacteria survive in agricultural soils used to grow sweet onions. The findings could help inform food safety risk management for produce growers.

items.title: New simulations connect the first stars to cosmic fingerprints still visible today
items.summary: Researchers have used some of the most detailed simulations yet of the early universe to investigate how the first stars and galaxies formed. items.title: Mulberry may reshape gut bacteria and influence metabolism
items.summary: Mulberry compounds may reshape the gut microbiome in ways that support intestinal health and metabolism, with some combinations showing especially strong effects in animal studies. However, the results vary depending on the plant part and processing method, and the benefits have yet to be confirmed

items.title: After 20 years, jet diffusion wakes detected in quark-gluon plasmas
items.summary: Boats passing over smooth water form a pair of diffusion wakes behind them veering off at a certain angle. Turbulence occurs along the line directly behind the boat, but the two diffusion waves are at a theoretical angle of 19.5° from the same line, for deep, ideally smooth water.

items.title: Who decides what time it is? The politics behind contested clocks
items.summary: Despite contentious local debates about time zones and seasonal shifts, University of Queensland research shows there is no official global time zone system.

items.title: NASA's Perseverance Mars rover finds groundwater, lakes, and hot fluids in one place
items.summary: NASA’s Perseverance rover has uncovered a surprisingly complicated history of water in Jezero Crater. Scientists expected the crater’s Margin Unit to contain lake sediments, but instead found ancient igneous rocks that were altered by water on at least three separate occasions.

items.title: Znanstvenici pronašli ranu poveznicu između fast fooda i depresije
items.summary: SMANJENJE unosa ultraprerađene hrane značajno ublažava simptome depresije, potvrđujući važnu vezu između kvalitete prehrane i mentalnog zdravlja.

items.title: Gene-silencing technology to protect forests from invasive pests
items.summary: A University of Kentucky forest entomologist is advancing a pest-control approach designed to target destructive forest beetles while minimizing effects on surrounding wildlife.

items.title: Wild crabapples have genetic potential to improve domestic varieties
items.summary: A bad apple doesn't always ruin the bunch. In fact, it might make the bunch a little stronger. items.title: Engineered nanostructured surfaces could offer a new way to limit marine biofouling
items.summary: Researchers at Sultan Qaboos University have developed engineered surfaces that combine microscopic patterns with zinc oxide nanorods to reduce the attachment of bacteria and microalgae—a process that contributes to biofouling on submerged marine and industrial equipment.

items.title: Black hole jets may decide the fate of entire galaxies
items.summary: Powerful jets from supermassive black holes can disturb star-forming gas far beyond a galaxy’s visible edge, leaving a glowing trail hundreds of thousands of light-years long. items.title: Snakes' appearances linked to how scary or appealing people find them
items.summary: Snakes can elicit a wide range of human responses, including fear, disgust, awe and admiration. Past studies suggest that both humans and nonhuman primates, such as monkeys and apes, tend to quickly notice snakes in their surroundings.

items.title: Pompeii’s 2,000-year-old eruption just gave scientists a better clock for Earth’s past
items.summary: Mount Vesuvius’ famous 79 CE eruption has given scientists a remarkably precise benchmark for dating events deep in Earth’s past. The improved technique could sharpen the timelines of volcanic eruptions, asteroid impacts, extinctions, and other major moments in geological history.

items.title: Watch Live: NASA’s Crew-13 could make the fastest U.S. trip to the ISS ever
items.summary: NASA’s SpaceX Crew-13 mission is scheduled to launch four astronauts to the International Space Station on October 1. The Dragon could reach the orbiting laboratory in just 7 hours and 50 minutes, making it the fastest U.S. spacecraft journey to the ISS in history.

items.summary: NOVO izvješće Copernicus upozorava na rekordno brzo zagrijavanje oceana, porast razine mora i zakiseljavanje.

items.title: One-third of world population exposed to harmful air pollution: Monitor
items.summary: Heat waves and wildfires combined with human-caused emissions this year to expose one-third of the world's population to extremely high levels of ozone pollution, a European Union report said Wednesday.

items.title: Paw-fect candidate: Australia finds new koala rescue dog
items.summary: The hunt is over: After trawling through dozens of applications, an Australian animal welfare group has found a successor to a hero hound credited with saving more than 100 koalas from fires.

items.title: Bats may have first evolved in Europe 65 million years ago
items.summary: A huge genomic and fossil study suggests bats first evolved in Europe around 65 to 60 million years ago before spreading across the globe.
